subject: K. T. Rama Rao (KTR)
guidance: Five personal Assembly victories across four career phases. Offices, attributed positions and bounded analysis remain distinct. Ten gender and forty era dimensions have explicit dispositions. Review counts describe registered fields, not historical completeness.

rows.Finding / value: Kalvakuntla Taraka Rama Rao, commonly K. T. Rama Rao or KTR; born 24 July 1976 in Siddipet, then Andhra Pradesh and now Telangana. Son of K. Chandrashekar Rao (KCR).
Sircilla MLA and BRS working president; a former Telangana minister. Working president is a party office and does not mean party president, Chief Minister or formal Leader of Opposition.

His biography reports an MSc in Biotechnology at Pune and an MBA in Marketing/E-Commerce at CUNY, followed by US work. The election affidavit also records postgraduate education; degrees and employment were not independently audited.
Five Sircilla victories: 2009, the 2010 by-election, 2014, 2018 and 2023. He retained his constituency when BRS lost government in 2023.

Entered the first Telangana ministry in June 2014; added urban and industrial responsibilities in 2016. After a gap following the 2018 election, returned on 8 September 2019 and served until the December 2023 change of government.
TRS became Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) in December 2022. This was a party renaming, not a personal party switch. His working-presidential appointment dates to December 2018.

Promoted Telangana’s technology and investment economy and helped develop T-Hub and related institutions. Government IT-export and employment series grew substantially; the evidence does not isolate his causal contribution.
MAUD responsibilities included building-permission reform and disaster response. The TS-bPASS rollout is documented; flooding and encroachment exposed continuing urban-management problems.

Weaver interviews credit public orders and local development while describing seasonal income and machinery constraints. Public procurement helped sustain work without resolving all livelihood vulnerabilities.

WE Hub provides a concrete women-focused institutional contribution. His 2024 remarks about women on buses drew criticism, a commission inquiry and an apology; programme design and public rhetoric require separate assessment.

Combines constituency cultivation, investor-facing communication and family-based party access. Following defeat he said excessive administrative focus and MLA-centred organisation weakened worker connections.

At the March 2025 Chennai meeting on delimitation, argued against centralisation and population-led dilution of southern representation. This is an attributed position, not an enacted seat-allocation outcome.

The High Court refused to quash the investigation in January 2025. A March 2026 chargesheet is reported; a discharge petition was filed later. The latest inspected hearing report adjourned the matter to 4 December 2026. No final guilt or discharge determination was established.

Questioned in January 2026 and denied involvement. October and 15 November reports anticipated a chargesheet naming him; a filed chargesheet or cognizance order against him was not inspected by the cutoff.

His strongest documented record combines repeated constituency victories with economic institution-building. Party defeat, concentrated family leadership, uneven local livelihoods and unresolved accountability disputes qualify celebratory accounts.
Original 2018 vote-share denominator, exact dates of some tenure boundaries, later court orders, and independent policy-impact evidence remain unresolved. Research Queue records specific next steps.
Evidence snapshot: 16 November 2026. Four career phases, 40 era-context items and ten gender dimensions. Prepared across 16–17 November; later events are outside scope.
Findings, review status and citation links appear first. Expand grouped columns for dates, counts, responses and qualifications. Claims and Evidence preserve field-level passage reviews.

Supported refers to the registered wording, including attribution or bounded analysis; it is not a completeness score. Not reviewed marks explicit research limitations. Blank values never silently mean zero or exoneration.

All five contests are direct Assembly elections. Party-wide and municipal campaigns appear elsewhere. Published shares are retained only for 2009, 2014 and 2023; 2010/2018 shares are withheld pending denominator reconciliation.

rows.Finding: T-Hub, WE Hub and T-Works supply concrete institutional evidence for his development-oriented reputation. Their existence is better established than their additional economic impact attributable to him.
Official export and employment growth supports a strong sectoral expansion narrative. Baseline inheritance and wider economic forces prevent a one-person explanation.
Five wins show durable Sircilla representation. The 2023 margin was much smaller than in 2018, and the 2009 victory had been exceptionally narrow.
Weavers’ support for public orders coexisted with seasonal distress. Both benefits and limitations appear within the same local reporting, without requiring a false all-success/all-failure choice.
rows.Assessment basis: Independent local reporting, not a survey

rows.Finding: The 2023 loss and 2024 parliamentary rout weakened the party he helped manage. His own explanation and Kavitha’s critique compete, but neither alone establishes a causal account.
Women’s enterprise support is a substantive policy mechanism; the all-male early Cabinet context and later bus-remark controversy complicate a uniformly inclusive image.
Formula E, surveillance and Nerella require distinct levels of responsibility and proof. Refusal to quash, investigation, opposition accusation and conviction are different stages.

A prominent second-generation leader of Telangana’s statehood party, he connects movement-era electoral politics to post-formation investment promotion and later opposition. His long-term legacy remains unsettled.
rows.Assessment basis: Provisional synthesis, not a greatness ranking
